messages.subject: Fwd: Explanation of error message?
parts:
Answer to a question about the "Your tree has Y fossil tips older than 0.6 my!" warning.  This will come up if you have fossils in your tree.  Read from the bottom...

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: XXX
Date: Thu, Feb 19, 2015 at 10:59 AM
Subject: Re: Explanation of error message?
To: Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org>


Hi Nick,

Thanks for that. Actually, the analyses weren’t working properly, but I seem to have solved that now - I found another error message that I had overlooked the firs time around. 

Of course, please post the issue - anything to help others with this.

Cheers,
XX

On 19 Feb 2015, at 15:11, Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org> wrote:

Hi XX!  Glad you're playing with things!  Given your data, you should ignore the warning.  It's just in there for people who either (a) put in an un-dated tree and don't realize that all the tips that don't match the age of the highest tip will be treated as fossils, or (b) people who have fossils very close to the present but not quite at the present (in which case they need to change the default fossils_older_than).

Can I post an anonymized version of this to the BioGeoBEARS google group to help others?

Cheers!
Nick



On Thu, Feb 19, 2015 at 8:39 AM, XX wrote:
Dear Nick,

Hope all’s well. 

I’ve been playing around with my BioGeoBEARS analyses and now have 22 time slices! Anyway, I’m getting the following error message -

'WARNING: Your tree has 43 fossil tips older than 0.6 my!
Make sure that 'fossils_older_than' is set to capture all of the fossil tips in your tree!
(default: fossils_older_than=0.6)’

Can you tell me what this means and what I should do about it? It looks like I should add ‘;fossils_older_than’ etc. to my script, but I am not sure where this should go and what value I should set it equal to. All my taxa are fossils, with only one of them having a stratigraphic range extending as far as 66 Mya, which is effectively time 0 in this analysis (all other taxa stop well short of this boundary).

Any advice would be greatly appreciated. 

Cheers,
XX
